title: Stonehenge
visualBrief: Current incomplete stone circle with three complete horseshoe trilithons, two broken groups, individually irregular sarsens, bluestones, fallen fragments, four outlying stones and low earthwork enclosure.
scaleBasis: Selected published dimensions where cited; remaining lengths and details are provisional artistic values.
geometrySource: Original deterministic Molen mesh generator; no third-party model or bitmap texture.
placementStatus: Reference coordinate only. Feature identity, footprint, orientation and bridge sectioning are unverified.

sourceFacts.reviewScope: Complete static medium-fi interpretation of the current surviving Stonehenge ensemble: seventeen outer sarsen uprights including the short fragment, six surviving outer lintels, three complete inner trilithons, two isolated inner uprights, fallen sarsen fragments, visible bluestones and stumps, a mostly obscured Altar Stone, Heel Stone, Slaughter Stone, both surviving Station Stones and low bank/ditch earthwork surface. Missing ancient stones and lintels are not reconstructed. Layout and condition were read from the current English Heritage2015 plan; above-ground profiles, heights, local tilts, fragmentation and joint dimensions are authored photographic interpretations, not survey meshes or exact stone-number identification. The first draft recipe remains unchanged and independently reproducible. Four browser levels retain every authored stone and the bank; chamfering and surface tessellation increase toward closeup. A shared sandstone graph stands in for sarsen silicified sandstone, and common raw basalt stands in for mixed bluestone geology. Lichen, carvings, graffiti and particular mineral grains are not copied. Plan controls and raw OSM stone outlines disagree locally because generalized aerial top outlines are not ground surveys; four distinct outlying stones constrain a rigid fit with no scale change. Registration tolerance5m/2Â° acknowledges this. Bank height and ditch depth are relative interpretations; the runtime host supplies absolute terrain and its slope may occlude or expose the setting. Below-ground sockets, buried fragments, excavation markers, fences, access paths, full Avenue, visitor center and the wider World Heritage Site are outside the exposed stone-and-earthwork asset. Physical phone/laptop timing is unmeasured.

geographicProposal.notes: English Heritage2015 current-site plan pixels and its25m scale/north arrow were actually inspected, separately from its ancient-phase reconstructions. Four fresh attributed OSM stone outlines identify Heel96, Slaughter95, Station91 and Station93 (way/133262440, way/133262443, way/377365047, way/377367000). Their centers rigidly fit the authored positions without scale change: anchor[-1.8262310128,51.1788579596],heading0.013739514043rad,maximum1.127m residual. Native+X points almost east and+Z almost south; the Heel Stone is east and north of the ring, resolving the sign. Whole earthwork identity is way37118074 Q39671 and is not used to stretch the32m stone ring into a120m building. Five-meter/two-degree registration is an accepted reconstruction, not a survey.
